subject: Software Lifecycle

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No CI pipeline builds or tests the code on push/PR

evidence.excerpt: (directory exists but contains no workflow files)

findings.recommendation: Add a GitHub Actions workflow (e.g. .github/workflows/ci.yml) that runs `dotnet restore`, `dotnet build`, and `dotnet test` on every push and pull request targeting main.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No documented release process (tagging, changelog, publish step)

evidence.excerpt: Increase the version numbers in any examples files and the README.md to the new version that this Pull Request would represent.

findings.recommendation: Document a concrete release process: how versions are tagged in git, how a CHANGELOG is updated, and how/where artifacts are published (e.g. NuGet, container registry, GitHub Release).

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: Two conflicting version numbers for the same product with no single source of truth
findings.recommendation: Pick a single version source of truth (e.g. drive the OpenAPI/appsettings version from the same MSBuild Version property, or vice versa) and bump it meaningfully with each release so the assembly version and the API's advertised version never diverge.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: Branching/review model is only partially documented and not technically enforced

evidence.excerpt: You may merge the Pull Request in once you have the sign-off of two other developers, or if you do not have permission to do that, you may request the second reviewer to merge it for you.

findings.recommendation: Name the branching model (e.g. trunk-based with a protected main), add a CODEOWNERS file, and configure a GitHub branch protection rule requiring passing status checks and the stated number of approving reviews so the policy is enforced, not just documented.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No build provenance, signing, or reproducible-build process

evidence.excerpt: (no workflow files; no build pipeline to attach provenance/signing to)

findings.recommendation: Once a CI pipeline exists, generate build provenance (e.g. GitHub Actions attestations) and sign published artifacts to reach a baseline SLSA level.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No automated or scheduled dependency updates
findings.recommendation: Add a Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) or Renovate configuration for NuGet so package versions in Directory.Packages.props are updated on a schedule rather than manually.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No SECURITY.md vulnerability-reporting policy
findings.recommendation: Add a SECURITY.md describing how to privately report vulnerabilities and expected response times.

findings.subject: Software Lifecycle
findings.title: No CHANGELOG or release notes

evidence.excerpt: (no CHANGELOG file present in the repository)

findings.recommendation: Add a CHANGELOG.md (e.g. Keep a Changelog format) and update it with each release alongside the version bump.

strengths.subject: Software Lifecycle
strengths.title: CONTRIBUTING.md documents a PR process and explicitly references SemVer

evidence.excerpt: The versioning scheme we use is SemVer (http://semver.org/).

strengths.subject: Software Lifecycle
strengths.title: Central Package Management gives a single, auditable source of truth for dependency versions
